data.body: decision-needed after RCA 2026-09-09: I reconstructed the concrete CI failure and found a design fork before a safe implementation. Evidence: run 34235734839 failed in the checkout step before repository validation; log lines show the helper first checked out the workflow dispatch/main ref from GitHub (`ref: 665d1d0480187380f82e59bd95af1f0c44274732`), then `git fetch origin refs/changes/34/2834/1` failed because GitHub does not expose Gerrit change refs, then Gerrit fallback `https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/rebar refs/changes/34/2834/1` returned HTTP 502. Gerrit recovered; recheck run 34236969595 passed and change 2834 merged as 02e0fae923d45329a3e1dc1921d70e19484401b8. I also fetched the third-party action source at the pinned SHA and confirmed this is its real algorithm: actions/checkout of `inputs.ref` (default `${{ github.sha }}`, i.e. the workflow ref), then mandatory Gerrit-refspec fetch from origin/Gerrit. Hypothesis confirmed for the checkout failure class: Verified depends on Gerrit being healthy because our mirror does not provide `refs/changes/*`, so transient Gerrit 502/504 can fail CI before tests. I did NOT claim or change code because the remediation choice is operator/design-sensitive. Options: (A) configure Gerrit→GitHub replication to publish `refs/changes/*`, preserving the current action and its intended mirror-first behavior; tradeoff: infra/Gerrit config change, but keeps CI YAML simple. (B) replace the action with an inline SHA-first checkout that fetches `GERRIT_PATCHSET_REVISION` from GitHub by object id then falls back to Gerrit and verifies FETCH_HEAD equals the dispatch SHA; tradeoff: portable in YAML if GitHub reliably serves pre-merge Gerrit objects by SHA, but that reachability must be proven/enforced. (C) accept Gerrit checkout 502/504 as infra-only and document `recheck` as the remedy; tradeoff: no code churn, but Verified remains sensitive to transient Gerrit outages. Recommended default: A if refs/changes replication to GitHub is acceptable; otherwise B only after an operator confirms pre-merge patchset SHA fetch is supported on the mirror. Specific question: should Verified be made independent of transient Gerrit HTTP availability by changing replication/checkout semantics, or should this remain an infra-retry class?
